questions.q: Rational roots of the equation $2 x^4+x^3-11 x^2+x+2=0$ are
questions.solution:
Given equation can be reduced to a quadratic equation.
$\therefore 2 x^2+x-11+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{2}{x^2}=0\Rightarrow 2\left(x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)+\left(x+\frac{1}{x}\right)-11=0$
Put $x+\frac{1}{x}=y2\left(y^2-2\right)+y-11=0\Rightarrow 2 y^2+y-15=0\Rightarrow y=-3$ and $\frac{5}{2}\Rightarrow x+\frac{1}{x}=-3, x+\frac{1}{x}=\frac{5}{2}\Rightarrow x^2+3 x+1=0,2 x^2-5 x+2=0$
Only 2nd equation has rational roots as $\mathrm{D}=9$ and roots are $\frac{1}{2}$ and 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The roots of the given equation $(p-q) x^2+(q-r) x+(r-p)=0$ are :
questions.solution:
Given equation is
$(p-q) x^2+(q-r) x+(r-p)=0$
By using formula for finding the roots viz: $\frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2-4 a c}}{2 a}$, we get
$\begin{aligned} & x=\frac{(r-q) \pm \sqrt{(q-r)^2-4(r-p)(p-q)}}{2(p-q)} \\ & \Rightarrow x=\frac{(r-q) \pm(q+r-2 p)}{2(p-q)}=\frac{r-p}{p-q}, 1\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The range of the function $f(x)=\sqrt{3 x^2-4 x+5}$ is
questions.solution:
$f(x)$ is defined if $3 x^2-4 x+5 \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow 3\left[x^2-\frac{4}{3} x+\frac{5}{3}\right] \geq 0 \Rightarrow 3\left[\left(x-\frac{2}{3}\right)^2+\frac{11}{9}\right] \geq 0$
Which is true for all real $x \therefore$ Domain of $f(x)=(-\infty, \infty)$
Let $y=\sqrt{3 x^2-4 x+5}$
$\Rightarrow y^2=3 x^2-4 x+5$ i.e. $3 x^2-4 x+\left(5-y^2\right)=0$
For $x$ to be real , $16-12\left(5-y^2\right) \geq 0 \Rightarrow y \geq \sqrt{\frac{11}{3}}$
$\therefore \quad$ Range of $y= \left[\sqrt{\frac{11}{3}}, \infty\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Solution of $2^x+2^{|x|} \geq 2 \sqrt{2}$ is
questions.solution:
$2^x+2^{|x|} \geq 2 \sqrt{2}$ ...(i)
Case I: $x \geq 0$, then Eq. (i) becomes
$2^x+2^x \geq 2 \sqrt{2}$
$\Rightarrow 2^x \geq \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow x \geq \frac{1}{2}$
Case II: $x < 0$, then Eq. (i) becomes
$2^x+2^{-x} \geq 2 \sqrt{2}$
$\Rightarrow t+\frac{1}{t} \geq 2 \sqrt{2}$, where $2^x=t$
$\Rightarrow t^2-2 \sqrt{2} t+1 \geq 0$
$\Rightarrow x \leq \log _2(\sqrt{2}-1)$
Also, $0 < \sqrt{2}-1 < 1, \log _2(\sqrt{2}-1) < 0$.
$\therefore$ The solution is
$\left. \left(-\infty, \log _ _2(\sqrt{2}- 1)\right)\right] \$ cup\$left[\frac{1}{2}, \infty\right)$

questions.q: Find the value of $a$ such that the sum of the squares of the roots of the equation $x^{2}-(a-2) x-(a+1)=0$ is least.
questions.solution: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation. $\therefore \alpha+\beta=a-2$ and $\alpha \beta=-(a+1)$ Now, $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=(\alpha+\beta)^{2}-2 \alpha \beta=(a-2)^{2}+2(a+1)=(a-1)^{2}+5\therefore \alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}$ will be minimum if $(a-1)^{2}=0$, i.e. $a=1$.

questions.q: In the real number system, the equation $\sqrt{x + 3 - 4\sqrt{x - 1}} + \sqrt{x + 8 - 6\sqrt{x - 1}} = 1$ has
questions.solution:
We have,$\sqrt{x + 3 - 4\sqrt{x - 1}} + \sqrt{x + 8 - 6\sqrt{x - 1}} = 1$

$\sqrt{( \sqrt{x - 1}{)}^{2} - 2 \times 2\sqrt{x - 1} + 4} + \sqrt{( \sqrt{x - 1}{)}^{2} - 2 \times 3\sqrt{x - 1} + 9} = 1$

$⇒ \sqrt{( \sqrt{x - 1} - 2{)}^{2}} + \sqrt{( \sqrt{x - 1} - 3{)}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ | \sqrt{x - 1} - 2 | + | \sqrt{x - 1} - 3 | = 1$

$⇒ | \sqrt{x - 1} - 2 | + | \sqrt{x} - 1 - 3 | = \left|( \sqrt{x - 1} - 2 ) - ( \sqrt{x - 1} - 3 )\right|$

We know that,

If $| x - a | + | x - b | = \left|( x - a ) - ( x - b )\right|$

then $( x - a ) ( x - b ) < 0$

$∴ ( \sqrt{x - 1} - 2 ) ( \sqrt{x - 1} - 3 ) < 0$

$⇒ 2 < \sqrt{x} - 1 < 3 ⇒ 5 < x < 10$

$∴$ Equation has& infinite many solutions.

questions.q: For the equation $3x^{2} + px + 3 = 0, p > 0$, if one of the roots is square of the other, then $p$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha, {\alpha}^{2}$ be the roots of $3x^{2} + px + 3$

$∴$ Product of the roots,&

$\alpha \cdot {\alpha}^{2} = 1 ⇒ {\alpha}^{3} = 1$

Again, $\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = - \dfrac{p}{3}$

$⇒ 1 + 1 = - \dfrac{p}{3}$ & (if $\alpha = 1$)

$⇒ p = - 6$

But $p > 0$

$∴ \alpha = 1$ is not possible.

If $\alpha = \omega$, then $\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = \omega + {ω}^{2} = - 1$

$∴ - 1 = - \dfrac{p}{3} ⇒ p = 3$

Again, if $\alpha = {ω}^{2}$, then

$\alpha + {\alpha}^{2} = {ω}^{2} + {ω}^{4} = {ω}^{2} + \omega = - 1$

$∴ - 1 = - \dfrac{p}{3}$

$⇒ p = 3$

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the equations $x^{2}-2 x-1=0,$ then what is the value of $\alpha^{2} \beta^{-2}+\alpha^{-2} \beta^{2}$
questions.solution: Since, \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^{2}-2 x-1=0\), then Sum of roots, \(\alpha+\beta=2\) and product of the roots \(\alpha \beta=-1\) Since, \((\alpha+\beta)=\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}+2 \alpha \beta\) \(\Rightarrow 4=\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}-2\) \(\Rightarrow \alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=6\) Now, \(\alpha^{2} \beta^{-2}+\alpha^{-2} \$beta^{2}=\frac{\alpha^{2}}{\beta^{2}}+\frac{\beta^{2}}{\alpha^{2}}=\frac{\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}}{(\alpha \beta)^{2}}$ \(\$Rightarrow\left(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}\right)^{2}=$6^{2}\) \(\Rightarrow \alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}+2 \alpha^{2} \beta^{2}=36\) \(\Rightarrow \alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}+2=36\) \(\Rightarrow \alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}=34 \ldots..$(\mathrm{i})$ \(\Rightarrow $\frac{\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}}{(\alpha \beta)^{2}}=\frac{34}{(-1)^{2}}=$34\) [Putting value of \(\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}=34\) from Equation (i) \(]\)
